newsitem.title: FRANCE: Text of Jospin victory speech in French election.
newsitem.headline: Text of Jospin victory speech in French election.

text.p: The following is the text of a speech by Socialist leader Lionel Jospin claiming victory after France's National Assembly runoffs on Sunday:
"Ladies and gentlemen, it seems that the French people have decided to elect, and with what clarity, a new majority to the National Assembly.

"...In the seventh district of the Haute Garonne, electors have just elected me as deputy. I thank them. I express my gratitude to the French men and women who have given their confidence to so many women and men who were candidates of the Socialist Party, of the left and the Greens.

"Let me express my joy, my pride and the feeling of responsibility towards them that we all feel. I imagine the immense joy of all those who voted for us, I realise and understand the disappointment of those who made a different choice on June 1.
"The electoral defeat of the RPR-UDF (ruling coalition) no doubt sanctions a failure of the government but even more a certain way of viewing politics which, in my view, is hopelessly out of date.

"The victory of the forces of change of the new majority in which each has taken part -- Radical Socialists, Communists, the Citizens' Movement, Greens, the Socialist Party... this victory crowns a campaign during which we have respected the French people, spoken with them, constantly made positive proposals for the future.
"Beyond the happiness felt by me and many others tonight, the overwhelming feeling that this very important election inspires for me is one of a deep demand from our people.
"It's not the demand of a 'right now' in which no one believes any longer. It's not the naive belief in promises which have been disavowed several times in the past.

"But it's a reasoned and pressing demand for real long-term progress for the French people, especially the least favoured among them. A demand for justice, a demand for a profound renewal of our public life and democracy, a demand for an economic and social policy put at the service of man, a demand for a reorientation of European construction -- which we favour -- and a demand for a scupulous attention to the problems French people meet in their daily lives.
"We will reply to this demand by listening to our citizens, by talking with them, by proposing innovative and realistic steps.

"We will have to mobilise all our energy, all our heart, all our competence, to carry out this different policy for which a new majority has just been elected. We will do it by keeping everyone in mind and by acting in the interests of France."
